strings.name: Christopher A. Pissarides
strings.summary: Pissarides studies unemployment, vacancies and search frictions. With Mortensen and others he developed matching models linking recruitment, job turnover and policy. A longtime LSE academic, he shared the 2010 economics prize with Diamond and Mortensen. He later co-founded future-of-work research, examining automation, AI and institutions supporting worker wellbeing.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through 13 November 2026; not a real-time news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Studied labor-market search and matching, explaining relationships among unemployment, vacancies and employment policy.

strings.highlights.h1.title: Unemployment and matching
strings.highlights.h1.text: With Mortensen and others, analyzed job creation, destruction and search frictions.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Future of work
strings.highlights.h2.text: Co-founded the Institute for the Future of Work to study technology and job quality.
strings.timeline.t1.title: AI and labor policy
strings.timeline.t1.text: Discussed AI, work and policy responses at the Royal Economic Society’s 2026 conference.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Future-of-work institute
strings.timeline.t2.text: Co-founded the institute with Naomi Climer and Anna Thomas.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Knighthood
strings.timeline.t3.text: Received a British knighthood for services to economics.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Economics prize
strings.timeline.t4.text: Shared the award with Peter Diamond and Dale Mortensen for markets with search frictions.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Job creation and destruction
strings.timeline.t6.title: Equilibrium Unemployment Theory
strings.timeline.t6.text: Published his systematic study of equilibrium unemployment.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Joined LSE
strings.timeline.t7.text: Moved from Southampton back to LSE’s faculty.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Economics doctorate
